txt: A strong gust of wind knocks into her. Then she shouts: "So what, pig? You gonna mock me now? I don't need this."
A wicked grin extends across her face.
Cindy picks the dirt out of her fingernails as you stand there, quiet and clueless. Without looking up, she says: "Ask something or piss off, swine."
Her lips move. "On fire?" she whispers to herself.
She hisses at the boat rocking gently on the coastal waves. "She'd flay my skin. Wear me like a mink the first chance she got." A mad grin spreads across her face. "Unless I got to her first."
She hisses: "That Ozonne whore. *Someone's* gotta keep an eye on her."
She hunches her shoulders and throws you a grim look. "I say, sod off. You don't have the technical skills to do that."
She juts out her hand, letting you examine the piece. Three red splotches have been shot at a diagonal across the surface. Tinier spots of various colours fan out from the same point of origin.
She looks you up and down. "I think everyone would rather you didn't."
She nods disdainfully toward the woman performing maintenance on the boat docked next to the pier.
She pretends to think about it for a moment. "No."
She shrugs. "But I'm still gonna write some damned good graffito on this wall."
She sighs. "You got me, pigshit. I don't make for a very good SKULL. I like animals too much. Simians and... pigs."
She squints her eyes...
She stares at you, fearlessly, waiting for a response.
She throws you a conspiratorial glance, then presses her finger to her lips and squints up at the sky -- as though straining to hear something in the distance.
The coat gets flung over her head as she braces for impact.
The girl erupts in a cackle that seems like it should belong to a much older woman...
"'I can only imagine the horrors,'" she mocks you in a squeaky voice. "I'm not your Channel 8 charity case. Sod off! No one here needs saving."
"*Signature*? Oh yeah, pigster. I sneezed while holding a wet brush. Paint flecked onto the canvas, and voila. You don't get more signature than that."
"A right communist. Who runs a *mega cool* and *very secret* meeting."
"Alright. Can't complain about that. You've got yourself a deal." She gives you the painting.
"An *underground cell*? My, my. Sounds big time..."
"And here I was trying to be polite. Just can't win with you pigs." Despite the sass, she puts the brush aside.
"And what do *you* know about politics?" She squints at you suspiciously.
"Anything else you want? I'm in a good mood -- but it won't last long."
"Anyway, I told him you'd never go in for the posters. Shame. I had some really good ones all planned out."
"Anyway, at least you convinced him to put up the posters. Good to see the old king covered in proper slogans. I saw one old bird nearly faint coming out of the Frittte."
"Art-ishoo."
"Ask away, pig man, but I don't promise to answer." Despite the sass, she puts the brush aside.
"Ask away."
"At first I thought that was just Uli putting me on, but then I saw Steb's cheek. You gave him a right love tap." She seems to approve.
"Awww, c'mon! I was just starting to have some fun."
"Be a good pig, now. No oink, no goods."
"Blah-blah. I already told you, I'm not for sale, piggo." She looks almost disappointed by your lousy offer.
"Blah-blah. I'm not for sale, piggo." She looks almost disappointed by your lousy offer.
"But boring. You're not using my lovely brush to spread boredom."
"But, fine, take the brush. I'm all out of fuel oil anyway." She drops the paintbrush at your feet.
"Can't you tell? I'm painting a beautiful mural. An aero-graffito visible from low orbit..."
"Cite me the statute that says you can't paint murals with fuel oil, and I promise I'll cease and desist."
"Come on! You really need to bring home the bacon." She chuckles.
"Could've been her. Small kid with giant white armoured hands. If you've seen one of them you've seen them all."
"Damn." She's almost ready to abandon the entire endeavour, but then changes her mind. "Well, it's also *art*. It's a conceptual illusion. Both the tool and the outcome."
"Didn't we all?"
"Do I need to come over there and pull on your curly tail? Squeal already!" She grins with power.
"Does anyone, in a city like this?" she replies wistfully, looking around.
"Don't come at me with that. You've got nuthin' on me. Not a pork scratching."
"Fat chance. But you *can* still do your part to revitalize the neighbourhood."
"Figures. All of you are liars. They're such sweet boys, though, aren't they? My sweet, sweet wannabe-SKULLS. They'll never be accepted. But their hearts are in the right place."
"Fine, take it, I'm all out of fuel oil anyway." She drops the paintbrush at your feet.
"Fine. I don't care about those wannabe-SKULLS -- and I don't care about your armour."
"From a guy on Boogie Street. Porta Rosa. Go there after midnight and you can get all kinds of funny things. Veterans of the People's Pile selling their stash."
"Fuck outta here," she bursts out laughing. "This 'let's get through this together' type of stuff doesn't work on me. Especially if it's coming from a pig!"
"Fuck-a-doodle-doo!" She stifles an outburst of laughter. "And what job would that be? Cutting you into rashers?"
"Go ahead and arrest me, officer. I swear I'll go peacefully." You can feel her smirk through the dark.
"God, if he isn't the saddest pig in the world..."
"God, you even talk the same now. Soon you'll be proofreading each other's homework..."
"Good call, piggo." She smiles to herself, satisfied.
"Good idea, piggies. Run along now, fuck her shit up good. Impound that boat while you're at it. I'd like to watch her *swim* back to Ozonne."
"Good little piglet," she says with words coated in butter.
"Guess this is what happens when two pigs put their heads together..." She seems slightly disappointed.
"Had a battery of tests just last week. I'm practically a patchwork of interesting critters. Kind of like a man o' war." Despite the attitude, she puts the brush aside.
"Have fun at your *underground meeting*, pig. Hope it's a *blast*."
"Have you ever tried your hand at graffito? When faced with a blank wall, most people write unimaginative stuff like *Pigs Go Home* and *Mona was here*."
"Have you got a crush on her? Aching for an opportunity to defend her honour?"
"Have you got any kids? Because you sound like the world's saddest dad right now."

"Have you noticed the *quiet?* Every so often, you might hear a gunshot pierce the air somewhere in Jamrock. But in Martinaise? No gunshots, no sirens. The people are languishing in boredom and complacency."
"He might."
"Heh. He was cooler before he started palling about with pigs..."
"Hello again, officers. Have you come to admire my mural?"
"Here. Happy?" The plastic looks sad and damaged, as if it's been ripped out of some bigger piece. A glitzy barnacle of colours covers its surface.
"Hey, up here, piggo!"
"Hold on. You didn't think it would be that easy, did you?"
"How sad. This little piggy doesn't know very much, does he?"
"Huh. I guess this little piggy has done his legwork after all..." She sounds slightly disappointed.
"I ain't helping no pigs fool honest, upstanding citizens. I'm not an *antisocial element*."
"I ain't no snitch, pigstein." She wrinkles her nose. "Go forth and forage in someone else's shit. No shortage of squealers in these parts."
"I don't believe it. I've never known those boys to have manners."
"I don't do 'happenings', I like to leave a *mark*." She looks at you as if she's ready to wound you, then stares at the red paint running down the wall.
"I don't do 'personal', if that's what you sickos are after. No navel-gazing pieces about what it means to be 'me'."
"I don't have a price. If I wanted to whore myself out, I'd go to Porta Rosa. Or better yet, I'd take you with me and pimp you out to some friends of mine."
"I have a weakness for animals. It's the animal-thing again. Damn it." She looks at you, a little sad suddenly.
"I haven't really started it yet. I'm waiting for the right words." She studies the wall, suddenly pensive.
"I like your idea. Should've thought of it myself. I don't need this kind of competition in my neighbourhood."
"I might."
"I think you didn't hear me. Why would I care?"
"I think you mean *boring*." She scowls. "Can't anyway. Technically, I'm banned. Not that it's ever stopped me getting my cigs."
"I thought I'd mix it up, you know, summon the forces of crime and social chaos -- with a wall-sized invitation."
"I thought you were a pig?" She squashes her nose with a thumb so it resembles a snout.
"I watched you go in, pig. You aren't telling me anything new."
"I'm Cindy the fucking SKULL -- what else do you want to know? Date of birth? Blood type? The last time I was tested for Hep C?"
"If I wanted to whore myself out for some *Nasenbonbon*, I'd go to Porta Rosa. Or better yet, I'd take you with me and pimp you out to some friends of mine."
"If you haven't been there, the village is a shithole down the coast from the main plaza." She waves her hand in a general westward direction. "Have a good time."
"If you say so. I like to think that my trigeminal nerve painted it."
"If you're *really* interested then I'm sorry," she whispers, "but I don't do anti-radiation drugs anymore so I don't know where to get them."
"In which case, they are not mine, and I have several witnesses who will corroborate my statement."
"Insult me all you want. You're still an art cop sans art materials."
"Intra-piggy conflict. Very cool..." For a moment her eyes appear to light up.
"Is that all you've got, piggy? Looks like the job market has failed me *once again*." Wind howls between the nearby apartment blocks. "No job, no art. What a pity."

"Isn't it part of your job to know all the illustrious personages 'round this shithole? She's the Wild Pines representative. Madame Professional Negotiator in the flesh -- and the flimsy linen." Her eyes narrow to slits.
"It doesn't *have to* do anything at all. Nothing does." She looks at the paint dripping down the wall. "Like me. Right now, I'm doing nothing at all."

"It's a sign! Better pay up or you'll anger the terrible beast from... what did you say?" She knows -- she just wants to ham it up. "The *threshold*. Careful now, I heard it has a soft spot for smoked pork."
"It's where they grow whores like her, and their whore men."
"It's where they grow whores like that one over there, and their whore men."
"Just look at this pig, sniffing about after-hours..."
"Just not me."
"Just that he's a real communist. Not like the play-acting you've been doing. The rest you'll have to see for yourself."
"Keep your money. What I want from you's better than gold..."
"Let me stop you right there, piggy," she interjects, raising her hand. "You have no idea, do you? No idea -- no brush. Fuck off."
"Listen to your partner, pig man. Keep your grubby hooves off little old ladies." Despite the attitude, she puts the brush aside.
"Look at me when I'm talking to you."
"Look at that, the pig's trying to break in without the passphrase. Tsk, tsk." The girl shakes her head slowly.
"Look at us, coming to an agreement. Who'd have thought?" A breeze blows strands of hair across her forehead as she leans into the balustrade.
"Lying is cool, I guess." She absent-mindedly paints a red streak on her left cheek.
"Madame Professional Negotiator in the flesh -- and the flimsy linen." She narrows her eyes. "Something morbid about old ladies trying to look young."
"Me -- a brickman? I haven't got the snout necessary to snuffle around your filthy yard." She spits out her tongue.
"Must have slipped my mind. You know how it goes." She gives you a lackadaisical shrug.
"Nice vest, officer. Taking art classes now?"
"No one cares, I know I don't. So sod off, pig! You've got nothing to change my mind."
"No-no. That's all the snitching Cindy the SKULL does for today. Actually, I don't even know why I told you what I just told you..."
"Not bad! I guess I'll take it." She holds back her excitement as she gives you the painting.
"Not him -- you. I want *you* to squeal for me, pork chop."
"Not particularly." Her eyes dart across the horizon. "I wanna keep this as brief as possible, you see. I want to return to painting the world *red*."
"Now, let's see if you're half as dedicated a communist as you say you are..."
"Of course you don't. Why do I even bother? Just cough up the money!"
"Oh really?" Her eyes flash like stolen coins under moonlight. "Good to know. That makes even easier pickings."
"Oh, I *know* they need an extra hand. Especially after that cargo went mysteriously missing last week."
"Oh, but I'm all out of fuel oil."
"Oh, but that's the way it should be. The natural order of things."
"Oh, did I hurt the very serious pig's feelings?"
"Oh, fine, I'll help. But first, I want something from *you*..."
"Oh, smart pig, because there *is*..."
"Oh, that's very nice. The little piggy wants to make sausages. Out of what, his little piggy friends?"
"Oink for me, piggy. Just once."

"Okay, whatever, piggy. Time to leech off each other like the parasites we are. Let me see what I've got..." She reaches into her heavy coat and pulls out a small piece of plastic coated thick with emulsion.
"On a first-name basis with her, are we? Piggy's moving up in the world."
"Ooh, little piggy knows the big words. What a waste of a perfectly good saucisson, stuffing it full of artspeak."
"Ooh, police brutality. That's the good stuff!"
"Ooh, the piggies have learned how to saunter up staircases. I didn't think you could do that with hooves. But -- here you are."
"Ooh. Not only have you found my address, you've discovered my biggest secret: I'm a coal miner."
"Or what? You'll shoot me down from this ledge and pry the bucket from my dead hands?"
"Pig's not half as dumb as he looks." She gives you a stately nod of approval.
"Piggy, I have no idea why I just told you that..." She looks at you, a little sad suddenly. "You look like a shaggy dog left in the rain for too long. I have a weakness for animals."
"Pigs and moles, eh? Sounds like something out of a children's fairy story."
"Poke your snout around sometime after 22.00 and you might just find them."
"Says you." She looks you up and down.
"See, Steban's a bit on the paranoid side. He's got all these *mega secret passphrases*, to keep out infiltrators and the like. You can't join the meeting without one."
"Shoot, piggy. It's what you do, isn't?"
"Sixty seven thousand reál. And your head on a silver tray."
"So did you two fancy each other?"
"So the little piggy is a big, bad communist now..."
"Sod off, pig man. Art is above the law." Despite the sass, she puts the brush aside.
"Something morbid about old ladies trying to look young."
"Something to think about next time you're driving around in your pretty little piggy carriage."
"Something to think about next time you're driving around in your pretty little piggy-carriage."
"Sorry, even with your fancy degree, you've got nothing to offer me."
"Sounds like you're just about to live out your self pity, not make a statement. I can't have shit art on my conscience."
"Sounds like you're really serious about meeting Steban. It's touching, sort of."
"Splat-splat!" From a dilapidated balcony, Cindy the SKULL gives Joyce the evil eye, her red paintbrush held to her throat...
"Splat-splat!" From a dilapidated balcony, a young girl in odd clothes gives Joyce the evil eye, a red paintbrush held to her throat...
"Squeal. Then maybe we can talk business."
"Steban's group meets only at night, in an old room in these apartments here. It just so happens you're in luck: Their weekly meeting is *tonight*."
"Stop quivering like jello, then you won't get fucked."
"Stop, pig. You're gonna make me heave..."
"Such is the bloody law of the bloody streets, you wankstain."
"Suit yourself." She tucks away the painting and closes her coat. You hear waves breaking on the nearby shore.
"Sure, I do. Steban trusts me."
"Sure, any time. Us *shit* artists have to help one another." She looks down at the wall and frowns. "Besides, I was out of fuel oil anyway."
"Sure, piggo." She reaches into her heavy coat and pulls out a small piece of plastic coated thick with emulsion.
"Sure. I know someone who'd love to talk that ideological stuff. You're looking for Steban."
"Thank you for passing on the message -- now run along, piggy."
"Thanks. I'm sure the inspiration will come to me now that I have an official RCM stamp of approval."
"That it? Alright. It all helps." She gives you the painting.
"That's enough. Off with you then." She makes a lazy shooing motion with her dangling hand.
"That's enough. Off with you, then." She makes a lazy shooing motion with her dangling hand.
"That's pretty fucked up, even for you, piggo."
"That's what I said, piglet."
"The government uses such a nice red colour to mark its heavy fuel oil. I simply couldn't resist."
"The streets will flow red once more. A great torrent, rushing down Rue d'Esperance. You wait and see." The girl stares at the sailboat by the pier.
"The whole point of graffito being on the street is so *everyone* can see it. No charge -- expression for all."
"Then get your brush from fucking *art*."
"Then you have time to find your own *fucking* brush."
"There, that wasn't so bad, was it?"
"There, there, piggy," she says in mock compassion. "I guess art just isn't really *you*. Cause you suck. In life. And in everything."
"They just might be. Rough stuff. If you take the ride, you'd be wise to buckle your little pig-belly up."

"They'd be delighted to get their hands on a squealing pink thing like you," she hisses. "Cut off your ears, make some pig soup out of them. Now sod off! You've got nothing to offer that would make me change my mind."
"They'll never be SKULLS. But..." She softens. "But their hearts are in the right place."
"This 'little persona' will grind you into a sausage if you don't stop. I'm not a sellout."
"This place is a sepulcher. We'll paint it red. We bring the raucous -- you bring the sirens."
"This place is severely lacking in havoc. Not even the occasional trash can fire to break up the tedium."
"Too bad, pork sausage, I don't sell my art. The whole point of graffito being on the street is so *everyone* can see it. No charge -- expression for all."
"Ugh, alright, piggy. I'll give you this one. I saw a little girl in the fishing village running around with military-grade hand-wear. Looked cute as hell."
"Ugh, alright, sad piggy. I'll give you this one -- I saw a little girl in the fishing village running around with military-grade hand-wear. Looked cute as hell."
"Uh, what are you doing...?" She looks disgusted, her individual facial features racing to be the most dramatic expression of her disapproval.
"Uh-oh, you're manipulating me!" She sounds almost fascinated by this discovery. "I do like a chance to rip off some stupid piggos. And I need a pack of cigarettes. And some paint."
"Use your little piggy brain. I'm sure *someone* will let you in..."
"Was that it?" She looks relieved. "Stop playing with your snout and let's get on with this so you can go back to your stinky sty. You still want this painting or what?"
"Watch your back, ungulate. You've got eyes on you."
"We apologize, but we're currently *not buying the entrapment you're selling*. Please call again later. Thank you." She smiles at her own joke.
"We rarely see pigs 'round here, though, just Union cads -- and my name's not Mona, so..."
"We weren't put on this earth to make your life pleasant, fuck-o."
"Well, if it's for *art*... But..." Her eyes narrow to slits. "What kind of art are we talking about?"
"Well, piggo, what do you make of it?" She sounds almost mocking, waiting for your reaction.
"Well, well. Seems like we're dealing with one tough pig. I'm impressed..."
"Well, well. Sounds like quite the snout you've got there..."
"What about it?" She tilts her head, waiting for your offer.
"What are you gonna do, climb up here? I'm unstoppable."
"What did you think I was using, aquarelles? Sucked it out of a cop's fuel tank myself -- back in Jamrock."
"What did you think I was using, aquarelles? This shit is pumped out of government vehicles."
"What do I care about some fucking tin egg shells?"
"What do you think I'm trying to paint here -- a mural for a better tomorrow? Why do you really need it?"
"What for?"
"What'd you think I was using, aquarelles?"

"What's that? The piggy's looking to get into the art market with a snappy business pitch?" Her eyes light up. "Watch out or you'll be auctioned off and face the chop!" She draws a line across her throat with a thumb.
"What's that? The piggy's looking to get into the art market?" Her eyes light up. "Watch out or you'll be auctioned off and face the chop!" She draws a line across her throat with a thumb.
"What, like your feeble business offer? Are you going to be the turning point in my shitty life story? A little fairy from above?"
"Whatever. I know someone who's into some pretty underground stuff. You're looking for Steban."
"Whoa! Calm it with that shit, cop. I don't have any art you can buy. Geez."
"Why would I? That would be so boring."
"Will you look at that! He's not just a pig, he's also a dog. Ain't got no bones for you, doggie." Despite the sass, she puts the brush aside and turns to you.
"Wow. That was easier than I expected. It's almost like you've been *wanting* to do it this whole time..."
"Wow. There's a proper *radical* piggy."
"Wrong. This is exactly how I treat my little brother."
"Yeah, I can see that. Cool mutations." She crosses her arms.
"Yeah, fuel. What'd you think I was using, aquarelles?"
"Yeah, whatever, Art Cop." A wide smile crosses her face. "Spaces, bodies, shit. Hit me with that lingo!"
"Yeah, whatever." A wide smile crosses her face. "Spaces, bodies, shit. Hit me with that lingo!"
"Yeah, you better keep walking."
"Yeah, you got me now. The dynamic between us has completely changed." She crosses her arms.
"Yeah... Not gonna hold my breath, piggy. You look like you'd suck. At... everything really," she quickly adds.
"Yeah?"
"Yes, Uncle Maynard. *Huge* trouble." She crosses her arms. "You're going to take out your metal detector and your collection of bottle caps and shrapnel."
"Yes, it really does..."
"Yes, my artistic integrity." It's impossible to tell whether she's being serious or not.
"Yes. I keep hoping a shaft will collapse on me, but somehow it never happens."
"You ain't seen nothing yet, piggy-boo."
"You call this a living?" She gestures to her surroundings. "Look around you, hog-man, we're all bleeding out on the slab."
"You heard your partner, piggy. I'm unstoppable."
"You really think I need to be high to see the world as art? Poor unimaginative piggy. How I wouldn't want to have *your* peepers."
"You should listen to your partner every once in a while. He's not so dim as you are."
"You think he'd allow me back into his store? No chance. Not unless he wanted to lose his stock all of a sudden."
"You're a real sad sack, you know that? Go ahead, then." She drops her paintbrush into the puddle below. "Art it up. Just try not to hurt yourself. And *no self portraits*."
"You're a real sad sack, you know that? Go ahead, then." She drops the paintbrush at your feet. "Art it up. Just try not to hurt yourself. And *no self portraits*."
"You're about to cry internally, aren't you piggy?" She utters a disapproving grunt. "Pathetic. Just give up, art isn't for you."
"Your partner here gets it. Anything else I can *not* do for you, gentlemen?" She gives you both a mischievous smile.
